name: Difficulty Settings
description: Puts back the Options dialog's Difficulty choice -- Easy, Normal or Hard -- as A New Home, The Lost Children and The Secret City have it. The Tree of Life already plays by a difficulty level, saved with each village (a village starts on Normal), and its rules are The Secret City's, but its Options dialog never shows the choice. With this patch the Difficulty row is drawn where The Secret City has it, directly above Game Speed, with the game's own radio buttons, words and font; Game Speed moves down a row and the dialog's frame grows by whole tiles, so the whole dialog stays on the screen with everything in it where it was. The choice is saved with the village. Easy: a new village starts with 300 more food; villagers never eat the extra food the other levels take; a fed, healthy villager tries to regain health on every check instead of about half of them; and villagers fall sick about a quarter as often. Normal (a village's level until you change it): above 8,000 food each villager's meal takes 2 more food three times in four; a starving villager loses health on about three checks in four. Hard: a new village starts with 99 less food; each villager's meal takes 2 more food three times in four at any food level; a starving villager loses health on every check. **The starting food only changes for a village made after you pick the level; the other rules follow the level at once.** **Needs no other patch; it works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Checked in a live game, windowed: the row's layout, every button, and the chosen level after a save and reload. Clicks in fullscreen have not been tried in a live game.** It is on by default; untick it to keep the stock dialog (a village then keeps the level it has). The companion is "VVFP Difficulty.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock dialog is shown.
behavior_changes: The Options dialog (drawing 0x41A5A0, clicks 0x41AD60) shows a Difficulty row at y+0x145: the heading and three radio buttons with Easy, Normal and Hard (strings 0x534 Difficulty, 0x535 Easy, 0x53A Normal (Game Speed's own), 0x537 Hard), the selected one the village's level (game-state field +0x170F4).

Game Speed's buttons, heading, labels and click areas move down 0x40 (64 pixels, the one tile the frame grows by; Difficulty sits 0x48 below Fullscreen and Game Speed 0x48 below Difficulty, as the stock 0x50 spacing does not fit the 600-pixel screen), to y+0x18D; the dialog's height becomes 0x23C, so its frame is one 64-pixel tile taller (576 pixels on the 800 x 600 screen); the frame, the Done button and the Music Tracks checkboxes are placed by the game from the frame, and the rows from the frame's top + 2 as in the stock dialog, so nothing else moves against them.

The stock handler's own three Difficulty click areas (0x41B159 / 0x41B187 / 0x41B1B9 write 0, 1, 2) move onto the new row's buttons, with the Game Speed buttons' insets; no click near Game Speed changes the level any more.

The level's effects are the stock game's own (starting food 0x41F3A3; food use, starvation and healing 0x4684E5..0x4686B0; sickness 0x4686B0 and 0x45E938): Easy: a new village starts with 300 more food; villagers never eat the extra food the other levels take; a fed, healthy villager tries to regain health on every check instead of about half of them; and villagers fall sick about a quarter as often. Normal (a village's level until you change it): above 8,000 food each villager's meal takes 2 more food three times in four; a starving villager loses health on about three checks in four. Hard: a new village starts with 99 less food; each villager's meal takes 2 more food three times in four at any food level; a starving villager loses health on every check.
explicit_non_changes: This row changes no executable bytes: VVFP Difficulty.dll verifies every stock byte it rewrites and writes them at run time; a different build of the game installs nothing.
No save byte, file or villager is written by the companion: the level is the stock field, written only by the game's own click handler and saved by the game's own save.
What each level does is unchanged: these are the stock rules, which already run on Normal in every village.
Every other row of the dialog (sound, music, voiceovers, music tracks, fullscreen) is drawn and clicked exactly as before.
